summary.oneLiner: A leading Indian designer, manufacturer and servicer of underground mining equipment, with a complementary construction equipment business, built on a five-decade engineering legacy.
summary.business: Eimco Elecon designs, manufactures and services underground mining machinery - side dump loaders, load haul dumpers, roof bolters, shuttle cars, a complete continuous miner package, universal drill machines, rocker shovel loaders and battery-operated MUVs/passenger vehicles - for India's coal and metalliferous mining operators. It also makes construction equipment (piling rigs, articulated loaders) for the domestic infrastructure sector, all manufactured at its Vallabh Vidyanagar facility and supported by a nationwide sales and service network.

currentContext.strengths: First Indian company to introduce Side Dump Loaders, Load Haul Dumpers, Universal Drill Machines and Rocker Shovel Loaders, fundamentally transforming mechanisation of underground coal and metalliferous mining - a pioneering legacy described as a formidable competitive moat|Long-standing institutional relationships with key mining industry players, supported by an extensive after-sales service network, anchoring its leadership position and generating high margins|Comprehensive Continuous Miner package (shuttle cars, roof bolters, CM3500, feeder breakers) positions it among the few players able to offer an integrated, one-stop underground mining solution|Early mover into fully battery-operated underground mobility (MUVs, MCAR-E passenger vehicles), sustaining technological leadership
currentContext.strategies: Diversify revenue streams by expanding the construction equipment business (indigenous piling rigs, developed under 'Make in India') to tap infrastructure-led opportunities such as metro rail, roads and urban development|Continue product portfolio expansion and indigenous R&D-led innovation, including scaling recently launched battery-operated underground mobility products|Leverage and strengthen the widespread service and distribution network across key mining regions to support timely customer support and higher equipment uptime|Pursue margin improvement through indigenisation and cost optimisation|Mitigate cyclical and geopolitical risks via diversification of the product portfolio, strengthening vendor relationships, and maintaining a prudent financial approach|Dividends are declared out of profits and recommended by the Board subject to shareholder approval, in accordance with the Company's Dividend Distribution Policy; no other explicit capital-allocation philosophy (buyback, debt-reduction or reinvestment policy) is disclosed in this bundle.
currentContext.expansion: During FY26 the Company undertook operational expansion initiatives aimed at strengthening its manufacturing capabilities and future growth prospects (no specific project, site or quantum named). It continued to expand its construction-equipment presence by scaling up indigenous high-end piling rigs (developed under 'Make in India') to diversify revenue streams into infrastructure-led opportunities such as metro rail, roads and urban development, with ongoing addition of new models to the portfolio. The Company also broadened its underground mining product line with the Continuous Miner 3500 (launched 2025) and, subsequent to the FY26 year-end, launched India's first fully indigenous battery-operated underground mobility products - the MCAR-E man-riding vehicle (15-person capacity, low-seam design) and the UV-A-BE multi-utility vehicle (10-tonne payload) - in April 2026.
currentContext.mdna: India's coal sector shows structural resilience: domestic coal production crossed the 1 billion tonne milestone for a second consecutive year, underpinning sustained long-term mining equipment demand|Underground mining is assuming increasing strategic importance for accessing deeper, geologically complex and land-constrained reserves as India pursues long-term production targets|Government policy initiatives - rationalisation of revenue-share mechanisms, waiver of upfront payments, and incentive structures for underground projects - are improving project viability and addressing high capital intensity/longer gestation of underground mining|Industry-wide transition toward mechanised, technology-driven underground mining (continuous miners, longwall systems, digital monitoring, remote operations) is expected to shift equipment demand toward modernisation, replacement cycles and technology upgradation rather than only incremental capacity additions|Increasing private-sector participation in commercial coal mining is likely to accelerate investment in modern underground equipment, particularly for technically challenging and deeper deposits|Geopolitical tensions and supply-chain/resource-security concerns are pushing India to strengthen domestic mining capabilities, favouring domestic manufacturers through localisation, technology partnerships and 'Make in India' policy support - though the same tensions also risk supply chain volatility, elevated input costs and longer lead times for imported components|Construction equipment industry sales declined ~2% year-on-year in FY26 due to a temporary slowdown in infrastructure execution, project deferments and geopolitical uncertainty; FY27 outlook is cautious but industry estimates project a return to moderate growth of ~2-4% in equipment volumes on improved project execution and gradual demand recovery|Union Budget's record infrastructure outlay of Rs.12.2 trillion is expected to sustain multi-year project pipelines across transport, energy and urban development, supporting the construction equipment business|Strategic focus on enhancing operational efficiency and expanding the product portfolio contributed to improved order inflows and execution during the year

risks.risk: Performance is inherently linked to the cyclical nature of the underground mining and construction sectors
risks.note: MD&A Risks & Concerns states any slowdown in capital expenditure by key end-user industries, particularly coal mining, may impact order inflows and execution timelines; with no subsidiary, JV or associate, the whole company rides one end-market's capex cycle.

risks.risk: Input-cost escalation on critical raw materials, chiefly steel and bought-out components
risks.note: The AR flags inflationary pressures and volatility in raw material prices, and says dependence on critical inputs such as steel and components makes the Company vulnerable to cost escalations, which may impact margins if not adequately passed on to customers. Operating profit margin already fell to 18.3% from 22.60%.

risks.risk: Geopolitical disruption of supply chains for imported components and technologies
risks.note: Risks & Concerns names ongoing global conflicts including the US-Iran War as a risk to global trade flows, energy prices and supply chain stability, leading to delays in procurement and increased logistics costs; the Chairman's outlook separately warns of supply chain volatility, elevated input costs and longer lead times for certain imported components and technologies.

risks.risk: Regulatory risk from changes in mining policies, environmental norms and government regulations
risks.note: The Company states such changes may impact project approvals and execution — a direct order-timing risk for a supplier whose customers need statutory clearances before mechanisation capex is released.

risks.risk: Intense competition from both domestic and international equipment players
risks.note: MD&A describes a highly competitive environment necessitating continuous innovation and cost competitiveness; the same 'Make in India' localisation push the Chairman cites as an opportunity also lowers the barrier for other domestic manufacturers.

risks.risk: Construction-equipment demand is contracting and the FY27 recovery is only modest
risks.note: The AR reports domestic construction equipment industry sales declined ~2% year-on-year in FY 2025-26 on a temporary slowdown in infrastructure execution, project deferments and geopolitical uncertainties, and calls the FY 2026-27 outlook cautious with industry estimates of only ~2-4% volume growth.

risks.risk: Uncertain tax positions, claims and contingencies carried in contingent liabilities
risks.note: The auditors treated this as a key audit matter, applying procedures over management's judgment of tax risks, estimates of tax exposures, the status of tax assessments and other litigations, and the probability of a negative result of litigation — i.e. an outcome that depends on tax-authority and court decisions outside the Company's control.

risks.risk: Very thin permanent workforce and key-personnel churn at the top
risks.note: The Company had 138 permanent employees as on March 31, 2026 for an engineering business dependent on specialised underground-equipment know-how; during FY26 an Independent Director (Mrs. Manjuladevi Shroff) and an Executive Director & KMP (Mr. Mukulnarayan Dwivedi) both ceased, with Mr. Kamlesh Shah appointed Whole-time Director from September 10, 2025.
